findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded on controller requests
findings.description:
The accelerator makes locale loading explicit (`lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:25-29`), and `I18n.translate` only loads `config.locale` (line 68). The site-default and `:en` fallbacks are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` in `set_locale`. Any path that never runs that filter gets fallback lookups against unloaded locales, which return nothing and yield "translation missing":

- **Sidekiq jobs:** `app/jobs/base.rb:151` sets `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale` in a process that never serves a controller request.
- **`with_locale` blocks:** `app/services/post_alerter.rb:138` and `lib/post_destroyer.rb:102` switch locale without loading its fallbacks.
- **Rake tasks:** `lib/tasks/db.rake:3,28` set the locale directly.

Fix: do the loading inside `I18n.translate`, e.g. `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale].each { |l| ensure_loaded!(l) }` in place of line 68, so it is independent of the entry point. The controller call then becomes unnecessary.

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain
findings.description:
The LRU key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`, but the result now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` via `FallbackLocaleList#[]` (`config/initializers/i18n.rb:17`). That setting is mutable at runtime and per-site in multisite.

- **Stale after a setting change:** nothing outside the accelerator calls `I18n.reload!`, so a string cached via the old site locale keeps being served until evicted.
- **Cross-site leakage:** in multisite, a string resolved through site A's default locale can be served to site B for the same user locale and key.
- **Cached misses:** combined with the finding above, a "translation missing" result computed before the fallback locale was loaded is frozen into the cache.

Fix: include the site default locale (or the joined fallback chain) in the cache key.

findings.title: No specs for the new fallback behaviour
`FallbackLocaleList#[]` edge cases
findings.description:
- **Dead `.compact`:** it cannot guard a nil site locale, because `SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym` would raise first; it only strips a nil `locale` argument.
- **No normalisation of `locale`:** a string such as the `locale: 'en'` passed at `app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:48` produces `['en', <site locale>, :en]`, which `uniq` does not de-duplicate. `locale && locale.to_sym` would fix it.
- **Site setting read on every uncached lookup:** each backend lookup now reads `SiteSetting.default_locale`. `lib/tasks/db.rake:3` (`rescue :en`) suggests that read can raise when the DB is unavailable, so `I18n.t` may now fail there too; I did not confirm this.

findings.title: `ensure_loaded!` nil-guard is inconsistent with the rest of the module
findings.description: `ensure_loaded!` lazily initialises `@loaded_locales ||= []` outside `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `translate` (line 68) and `load_locale` (line 48) assume it is already set. Either the guard is unnecessary, or the other two can raise `NoMethodError` on nil. The method also duplicates the `include?` pre-check that `load_locale` already does under the mutex. Initialise the ivar once at definition time and have `ensure_loaded!` delegate.

findings.title: Initializer structure and conventions
findings.description:
- **Ordering by comment:** the file relies on `# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb`, whereas ordered initializers in this directory use numeric prefixes. It works only because `i18n.rb` sorts after the numbered files.
- **Two ways to name the backend class:** line 5 includes into `I18n::Backend::Simple` and line 9 into `I18n.backend.class`. Use one.
- **Unneeded `Hash` inheritance:** `FallbackLocaleList < Hash` overrides only `[]`, so `fetch`, `key?`, `each` and the rest silently behave as an empty hash. A plain object responding to `[]` would be more honest.
- **Misplaced responsibility:** `ensure_loaded!` on the list reads the global `I18n.locale`, which belongs with the loader in the accelerator rather than on the fallback list.
